deep.reconstruction:
Page 35 (dated 15.11.66) is the opening of the lecture notes for Grothendieck's IHES talks on crystals. These talks became 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (notes by I. Coates and O. Jussila, in Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas, 1968). The page sets up the motivation.

(1) Recall of the comparison theorem. For a smooth complex algebraic variety X, the singular cohomology H^*(X^an, C) is computed purely algebraically as algebraic de Rham cohomology, the Zariski hypercohomology H_DR(X) = H^*(X, Ω^•_X). This is Grothendieck, 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties', Publ. IHES 29 (1966).

(2) This definition makes sense over any base field, but it has drawbacks:
- It is tied to differential forms, hence to non-singular varieties.
- Over a field of characteristic p>0, the cohomology is a vector space over a field of characteristic p. So it cannot serve as a Weil cohomology with characteristic-0 coefficients.

(3) Hence the desire for a 'p-adic' cohomology for varieties in characteristic p. It should play the role that ℓ-adic cohomology plays for ℓ≠p, giving Betti numbers, etc.

(4) Relative version. For a relative prescheme f: X→S:
- Ω^1_{X/S} is defined, and Ω^•_{X/S} = Λ^• Ω^1_{X/S} carries the exterior derivative.
- One defines H_DR(X/S) = H^*(X, Ω^•_{X/S}) and the sheaves R f_*(Ω^•_{X/S}).
- The right-hand bracket notes these are coherent / locally free when f is proper and smooth.
- A boxed marginal reminder says to mention compatibility with base change when f is smooth.

This prepares the next pages. There, X_0/k is lifted to a proper smooth X over W(k), H_DR(X/W) is formed, and the Washnitzer–Monsky idea is reinterpreted: the cohomology is independent of the lift up to canonical isomorphism. That leads to crystalline cohomology.
errors: Base change: Rf_*Ω^•_{X/S} is a perfect complex whose formation commutes with arbitrary base change in the derived sense when f is smooth and proper. However, the individual sheaves R^i f_*Ω^•_{X/S} need not be locally free, nor commute with base change, without extra hypotheses (e.g. characteristic 0 with Hodge–de Rham degeneration, or torsion-freeness). The marginal note 'compatible avec chgt de base si f lisse' is correct only in the derived/complex sense or under such hypotheses.
Minor: 'propre' is needed for coherence; smoothness alone does not give finiteness of R f_*. The note seems to state this correctly in the bracket.

ideas.what: Algebraic de Rham cohomology computes complex cohomology of smooth varieties
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's algebraic de Rham comparison theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1963 letter to Atiyah; Publ. IHES 29, 1966)
ideas.where_published: On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties, Publ. Math. IHES 29 (1966)

ideas.what: Inadequacy of de Rham cohomology in characteristic p (char-p coefficients) and the need for a p-adic Weil cohomology
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Relative de Rham cohomology H^*(X, Ω^•_{X/S}) and R f_*Ω^•_{X/S}, with coherence for proper smooth f and base change
ideas.modern_name: Relative algebraic de Rham cohomology (Gauss–Manin setting)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes; Publ. IHES 29

deep.surprise_reason: Standard introductory material for the 1966 crystals lectures, all of which appears in the published 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes'. Nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Celle-ci a un sens pour un préschéma [?] quel[-c-] schéma [?] sur un corps quelconque' reads more like 'Celle-ci a un sens pour n'importe quelle [variété/schéma] sur un corps quelconque'.

In 'le corps de [-définition-] base', the crossed-out word looks like 'coefficients' rather than 'définition'. The intended sense is that the base field of the cohomology theory is of characteristic p>0, i.e. the coefficients are in characteristic p.
The marginal box reads approximately 'dire que c'est compatible avec chgt de base si f lisse...'.
The bottom-right bracket reads approximately '[coh. si f propre ; loc. libres si f propre, lisse ...]' rather than a repeated 'f propre et lisse'.
